content: One must never do wrong in return, nor mistreat any human being, no matter what one has suffered at their hands.
author: Socrates
story:
This insight touches directly on the messy reality of human nature. Hardship is not an unfair interruption to your real life—it is the very forge in which character is tempered. No one develops deep wisdom, empathy, or stamina by cruising down an easy path without resistance.

Socrates understood that real peace is never won by escaping the world or blaming external circumstances. Like a tree that develops deeper roots when buffeted by winter gales, your past trials gave you a reservoir of strength you didn't know you possessed. You are more durable than your anxious thoughts give you credit for.
reflectionPrompt: How does adopting this philosophical view alter the way you handle current friction?
